ownership_reason: Only the gold decides, for each form control, whether it submits and computes the value of the pairs it adds (the value attribute, a textarea's text, 'on' for a checked checkbox or radio button without a value, a select's selected options). Hop 1 creates the list and returns it; hops 2-4 pass the controls on unchanged, as their javadoc says, and the list along. A caller cannot supply a textarea's value, which the gold reads from the control itself, except by writing an attribute into the document (a side effect against the hops' and the facade's documentation); once the gold has appended six= with an empty value, the text can come back only if a caller rewrites the gold's pair from the control's text, a second implementation of the gold's value rule. The gold's javadoc promises the pairs that the controls submit; a textarea submits its text. The convention is pinned outside the gold by production code doing the same step: Element.val() (a textarea's value is its text, otherwise the value attribute), Element.val(String) and Elements.val(), with the passing tests HtmlParserTest::handlesTextArea, HtmlParserTest::preservesSpaceInTextArea and ElementsTest::val, and through the chain FormElementTest::adoptedFormsRetainInputs and FormElementTest::usesOnForCheckboxValueIfNoValueSet.
